title: Transcorrelated Random-Phase Approximation
authors: Abdallah Ammar, Enzo Monino, Anthony Scemama, Emmanuel Giner, Pierre-François Loos
abstract: We extend the random-phase approximation (RPA) to the non-Hermitian transcorrelated (TC) Hamiltonian, which explicitly includes three-body interactions generated by a Jastrow correlation factor. We consider both the direct RPA (dRPA) and RPA with exchange (RPAx). We apply the resulting TC-dRPA and TC-RPAx methods to calculate ground-state correlation energies and vertical excitation energies for atoms (\ce{He} and \ce{Ne}) and small molecules (\ce{H2O}, \ce{NH3}, \ce{CH4}, and \ce{H2CO}). For ground-state correlation energies, the TC treatment substantially improves accuracy and accelerates basis set convergence, reducing errors by nearly an order of magnitude relative to conventional RPA calculations. By contrast, it yields only marginal improvements in vertical excitation energies. We attribute this limited effect to the ground-state optimization of the Jastrow factor, which does not adequately capture the distinct electronic character of excited states. These results establish TC-RPA as an accurate and computationally efficient approach to ground-state energetics, while highlighting the need for state-specific Jastrow optimization to achieve reliable descriptions of excited states.
summary: This paper introduces the Transcorrelated Random-Phase Approximation (TC-RPA) to enhance electronic structure calculations by incorporating explicit three-body correlation effects via a Jastrow factor. It demonstrates that TC-RPA provides substantial accuracy improvements for ground-state energies in atoms and molecules, making it an efficient tool for ground-state energetics. However, the authors caution that state-specific optimization is needed to accurately model excited states.
main_problem: The primary goal is improving electronic structure calculations by addressing the slow basis set convergence of standard Random-Phase Approximation (RPA) due to short-range electron correlation effects.
main_result: The Transcorrelated RPA (TC-RPA) significantly improves accuracy and accelerates basis set convergence for ground-state correlation energies, but only shows marginal improvement for vertical excitation energies.
method: The authors extend the RPA formalism to a non-Hermitian Transcorrelated (TC) Hamiltonian by incorporating three-body interactions via a Jastrow correlation factor. They apply this using both direct and exchange variants of the approximation.
model_or_system: Calculations are performed for atoms (He, Ne) and small molecules (H2O, NH3, CH4, H2CO). The theory utilizes an Equation-of-Motion approach applied to the non-Hermitian TC Hamiltonian, requiring a biorthogonal formalism.
key_observables: Ground-state correlation energies and vertical excitation energies.
important_parameters: The Jastrow correlation factor, which is optimized for the ground state.
main_assumptions: The primary limitation noted is that optimizing the Jastrow factor only for the ground state limits its effectiveness in describing excited states.
figures_summary: Not specified by notes; however, a comparison figure mentioned suggests TC-RPA accelerates basis set convergence compared to standard RPA calculations for ground-state energies.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by extending RPA to the non-Hermitian TC Hamiltonian. It then applies this method to calculate correlation and excitation energies for various molecules, culminating in a comparison of results showing differential improvements between ground and excited states.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles highly correlated electronic structure problems using advanced many-body techniques (RPA extensions), which is central to understanding chemical bonding and material properties relevant to AMO physics.
